title: Crowd in capital with targeted investment strategies

blocks.text: Theme 3.1 · Investment, inclusion and sustainability · Focus area 15
Crowd in capital with targeted investment strategies

The province has a capital pipeline for airports, ports, roads and rail, but none of it reaches tourism product, bookability, accommodation depth or community assets, which is where the growth case needs investment.
**December 2025.** Crowd-In Capital with Targeted Investment Strategies (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64).

**October 2026: Validated, on inference.** No pipeline. The Infrastructure Report's pipeline and gap-closure tables drove the disposition, with the stakeholder view that funding sits below peers and the Chilean and New Zealand benchmarks. The reason is an inference: the report lists a large capital pipeline, and its gap columns show that none of it reaches tourism product.

blocks.caption: Capital is committed to gateways and transport, and each district's tourism gaps carry no committed capital.
blocks.source: Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026 (IR; the ~R11.3bn CTIA headline itemises to R9.94bn on p103); Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026 (SIR); SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026 (SCIP). No deliverable gives a Western Cape tourism funding-gap figure.
rows: About R30bn or more planned: ~R11.3bn at Cape Town International, R20bn for the V&A Granger Bay expansion and R3.3bn for MyCiTi Phase 2; SME bookability and township product sit outside every capital programme
R310m George terminal by 2028; Cape Winelands Airport ~R8bn private phase 1, with funding not yet locked in
No committed capital for West Coast accommodation and payments, De Hoop accommodation, Whale Coast bookability, Overberg year-round product or Route 62 accommodation
Of the port capital listed, only the R22m Mossel Bay reception facility is for cruise
Western Cape tourism funding is materially below peer destinations, and a tourism levy and blended finance are under consideration
Kliptown's Walter Sisulu Square cost R160m to R180m before an operator and drew about 4,000 museum visitors a year by 2017

blocks.text: The instrument this entry calls for was planned and not delivered. The Inception Report scoped an investment opportunity framework that would score gaps against return, jobs and inclusion, with a roadmap of quick wins, medium-term plays and long-term moves (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p18, p20). The gap-closure tables are its input [Western Cape tourism funding against the peer set: DEDAT and Wesgro budget data needed].

Wesgro should build the tourism investment pipeline the gap tables imply, and commit capital only where demand has been shown. The Inclusion Plan's rule applies across the portfolio: invest after demand, and attach a maintenance and marketing covenant to any public asset (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p31, p15). The benchmarks offer the vehicles: Chile's private concession for its gateway airport and New Zealand's route incentives tied to bookings (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p26, p54).

rows: Build a tourism investment pipeline from the gap-closure tables, scored for return, jobs and inclusion, and take it to investors
Prepare investment cases for mid-scale and conference-capable hotels in secondary nodes and for accommodation at De Hoop and on Route 62
Scale Cape Town Air Access's route fund into the public-private air access fund, with ring-fenced corridor budgets (focus area 7)
Air Access; DEDAT; City of Cape Town; private sector
Test a tourism levy and blended-finance vehicles for destination management and mobility
Attach covenants to public assets before re-letting or upgrading them, and invest in community assets only after demand is proven
Hold ACSA, PRASA and Transnet to their published capital dates, and add tourism use to the port plans

blocks.text: Chile funded a ~US$900 million expansion of its gateway airport through a private concession awarded by its Ministry of Public Works (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p26). Melbourne's event-led demand drew 21% growth in hotel rooms, 5,000 new rooms and the entry of global hotel brands (p18).
**Initiative I14**, tourism investment pipeline (section 4.3). **Indicator** T2-20 pipeline projects at financial close at outcome level (section 5.2).
